rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act – Grounds for removal of tenants
rules.requirement: A residential tenant may be removed by the Superior Court only on one of the enumerated good-cause grounds. These grounds are: nonpayment of rent; disorderly conduct after written notice; willful or grossly negligent damage; continued substantial violation of reasonable rules or lease covenants after written notice; failure to pay a lawful, non-unconscionable rent increase; code-violation board-up, demolition or compliance; correcting an illegal occupancy; permanent retirement from residential use; refusal of reasonable lease changes; habitual late payment; condominium or cooperative conversion; owner or buyer personal occupancy in limited cases (condo or co-op owners of 3 or fewer units, or buildings of 3 or fewer units); termination of employment-based tenancy; certain drug, assault/terroristic-threat or theft convictions or civil findings; and human trafficking. Lease expiration alone is not a ground. Some grounds require prior written notice to cease. Some grounds (g, k) bar a warrant for possession until relocation and conversion statutes are complied with.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for enumerated good causes (subsections a–r); no termination without cause
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental premises, including mobile homes and mobile home park land. Excluded: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units; hotels, motels and guest houses rented to transient or seasonal guests; certain units held in trust for, or occupied by, an immediate family member with a developmental disability.
rules.exemptions: Excluded: owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units; hotels, motels or guest houses rented to transient guests or seasonal tenants; a unit held in trust for, or permanently occupied by, an immediate family member of the owner who has a developmental disability. Senior citizen and disabled protected tenants, and qualified tenants under the Tenant Protection Act of 1992, have additional protection against conversion evictions.
rules.interaction: The rent-increase ground (f) requires that the increase not be unconscionable and comply with any municipal rent ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: No lessee or tenant or the assigns, under-tenants or legal representatives of such lessee or tenant may be removed by the Superior Court from any house, building, mobile home or land in a mobile home park or tenement leased for residential purposes, other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units
